A closed_error also doesn't reveal which check refused it, since both _error and the new _stream_closing raise the same exception.

issues.title: Failed BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL aborts the whole process via sink_impl's destructor assert
issues.verdictReason: If BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL(client_factory.hooks.size(), 2u) fails it unwinds the stack and destroys the still-open sink; sink_impl::~sink_impl (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:932-936) runs SEASTAR_ASSERT(sink_closed()), and SEASTAR_ASSERT calls assert_fail which aborts the process (include/seastar/util/assert.hh), so this failure mode kills the whole test binary instead of reporting a normal Boost.Test failure.
issues.scopeReason: New test code added by the PR.

issues.title: A hook throwing a non-closed_error exception may leave the test parked with no deadline
issues.verdictReason: If stream_send_empty_frame() throws something other than closed_error it propagates uncaught out of the test lambda, unwinding local variables including test_sink_state st; since st.release_close is a seastar::shared_promise, its destructor would normally deliver a broken_promise to the parked close() continuation and unblock it rather than hang forever, but confirming whether that unblocks cleanly or leaves other state corrupted would require instrumenting the exact destructor order, which I did not have budget to run.
issues.scopeReason: New test code added by the PR.

issues.title: New stream_close() queue-drain branches (pending entry, exceptional drain, mid-entry…
issues.verdictReason: sink_impl::close (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:903-929) awaits con->send(eof marker) to completion before calling close_sink(), so by the time connection::stream_close() runs, _outgoing_queue_ready is already a resolved, non-exceptional future in every path the new test exercises; the three new branches at src/rpc/rpc.cc:562-569 (an entry still queued, an exceptional queue_drained, peer disconnect mid-entry) are never hit.
issues.scopeReason: These branches were added by this PR's fix and are only reachable through it.

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r62-ironweav: sink_impl::close awaits its eof send() before close_sink(), so queue_drained is always already ready in the test. Three cases are never exercised: an entry still queued when stream_close() starts, an exceptional _outgoing_queue_ready, and the peer disconnecting while an entry is pending.

issues.title: New comment misstates when _outgoing_queue_ready becomes exceptional
issues.verdictReason: connection::send's continuation (src/rpc/rpc.cc:333-339) catches a failed send_entry, calls abort(), and still unconditionally calls p->done.set_value() (not set_exception), so a failed send does not make _outgoing_queue_ready exceptional as the new comment implies; it only becomes exceptional via connection::withdraw(it, ex) from stop_send_loop, or via the front entry's it->done.set_exception(ex) when _negotiated is still engaged.
issues.scopeReason: The comment was added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: Comment is wrong about when _outgoing_queue_ready becomes exceptional

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r62-ironweav: A failed send_entry calls abort() and then p->done.set_value(), so _outgoing_queue_ready does not become exceptional when an entry fails, contrary to what the comment implies. It is exceptional only via stop_send_loop with _negotiated engaged, or when _negotiated itself failed.

issues.title: No guard against a second make_sink() call lets an unclosed sink silently bypass the 'is…
issues.verdictReason: source<In...>::make_sink (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:999-1001) unconditionally constructs a new sink_impl and sets the connection's single shared _sink_closed=false with no check for a pre-existing open sink; calling it twice and closing only the second sink flips _sink_closed back to true, so dropping the first, truly-unclosed sink no longer trips sink_impl::~sink_impl's SEASTAR_ASSERT(sink_closed()) (rpc_impl.hh:932-936), silently defeating the doc's claim that 'dropping an unclosed sink is an error'; a second close() does correctly return stream_closed (rpc_impl.hh:911-913). The doc's 'is an error' phrasing also undersells that the real consequence is a process-aborting SEASTAR_ASSERT.
issues.scopeReason: The absolute doc claim was added by this PR; it doesn't fully hold given pre-existing make_sink() behavior.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: No guard against a second make_sink() call; doc's 'dropping unclosed sink is an error' claim is undermined

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r62-ironweav: make_sink() has no guard against a second call, and _sink_closed is connection-wide, so a second close() returns stream_closed ('double close') and dropping it unclosed does not assert, contradicting the doc's claims about closing on the last reference and dropping an unclosed sink being an error. The doc phrase 'is an error' also hides that the real consequence is a process-aborting SEASTAR_ASSERT.

issues.title: Peer EOF/error tears the socket down without the app closing both halves, contradicting…
issues.verdictReason: On peer disconnect the receive loop sets _error=true and calls stop_send_loop (src/rpc/rpc.cc:1065-1066), which immediately calls fd.shutdown_output() (rpc.cc:201) and then closes write_buf (rpc.cc:225-232), all independent of whether the application ever called sink.close() or drained the source to eof; this physically shuts the connection down without both app-level halves having been closed, which the doc's absolute 'shut down only once both halves are closed' sentence (doc/rpc-streaming.md:115) does not account for.
issues.scopeReason: The absolute doc claim was added by this PR and doesn't cover the pre-existing abort/error teardown path.

issues.title: Synchronous ordering of the three new stream_close() statements is undocumented

issues.title: An exceptional queue drain is swallowed when closing the write buffer
issues.verdictReason: The behavior is real (queue_drained.then_wrapped ignores any exception via f.ignore_ready_future() and closes write_buf regardless), but it is in fact documented by the adjacent new comment at src/rpc/rpc.cc:566-567, even though that comment's explanation of when the drain becomes exceptional is itself slightly inaccurate (see I6); treating this as a separate undocumented-behavior finding double-counts I6.
issues.scopeReason: New code and its accompanying comment were added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: An exceptional drain is swallowed silently and undocumented

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r62-ironweav: sink.close() reports success unless write_buf.close() itself fails, silently swallowing an exceptional drain, and this behavior is not documented.

issues.title: PR body overstates the new test's determinism and loosely describes the queue-drain…
issues.verdictReason: Empirically verified: with the _stream_closing guard in connection::send() disabled (simulating pre-fix behavior) and the rest of the series intact, 30 runs of test_stream_send_after_stream_close under the test's actual default (-c 2) produced 1 unexpected pass out of 30, directly contradicting the PR body's claim 'the new test fails without the first commit'. Separately, 'chaining on _outgoing_queue_ready the way send() does' is an imprecise description: stream_close() takes a one-shot std::exchange snapshot of the current value, not send()'s self-extending chain.
issues.scopeReason: This is the PR's own description text.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr2: PR body's description of the wait mechanism is imprecise and overstates test guarantees

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r62-ironweav: The PR body says the fix chains on _outgoing_queue_ready 'the way send() does', but the code actually exchanges it for a ready future. The body also asserts determinism and fails-without-fix validation, which the test-gap finding about rpc_test.cc:2017 calls into question.
